Not conclusively. No fire detections intersected the asset (ASSET-F02) in the data that was available, but the evaluated period (25 Sept to 25 Oct 2026) was not fully covered.

All four sensors (VIIRS S-NPP, NOAA-20, NOAA-21 and MODIS) cover 25 Sept to 24 Oct. None of them covers the final day, 24 to 25 Oct, because it falls after the latest near-real-time file update (the day was either still in progress or not yet published).

The run's own rule is that every day must be covered for a sensor to count as covered. By that rule, no sensor fully covers the period.

So the accurate statement is: no fire detections on the asset from 25 Sept to 24 Oct, and the last day is unchecked. A fire on that day can't be ruled out. Re-running once the data is published would close the gap.

Satellite detections also only capture fires active during overpasses, so small or brief fires may be missed.
